meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.

"The zero stands." On a machine's guess. The people who sell that software tell schools not to punish a student on it alone, and I have their guide in my bag, so what do you have besides a percentage?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you're relying on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he wrote it somewhere else and pasted it in. Did you put any of this to him before the zero went in?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.

I'll ask him for the other document. A wrong line is a mistake, the kind a seventeen-year-old copies off a bad study site at midnight. And whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears a word of it.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
A student changing his argument between an outline and a final draft is called thinking, Hale. And you went straight past what I said about his record.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
So you did speak to him before it went in. Five minutes cornered by a teacher and a boy goes blank, and all I have for it is your own notes. Is anything on his record right now, yes or no?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes under a clock is not a weekend at home. I asked you a yes or no question, and it wasn't about commas.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

Then he does the rewrite under 4.4, to put this behind him and for no other reason. Private, nothing on file, and I have it in writing tonight. Whether anything sits on his record today goes in my email, and you'll answer it there.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school, marked within two days. Put both in tonight's email. Who is in the room with him while he writes?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. And the name of whoever sits in that room with him goes in the email, since you didn't answer me.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday after school, marked within two days, that if it shows the learning its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require your written answer on whether anything is on his record today, and the name of whoever will supervise him while he writes. You said I would have all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, with its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, and all of it in writing tonight. She still wants an answer on whether anything is on his record today and the name of whoever supervises him. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.

What moved her: you showed the version history with its dates and times, then answered her paste-in defence by offering to look at any other document and its history. That gave her something dated that she could check herself, and left her defence with nowhere to go.

What cost ground: you opened with the checker score and told her the zero stands. To her that is a machine's opinion she cannot check, and it kept her at her opening position until you started again.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history came close, with the document created at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28 and the text arriving at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM. She wrote the times down and went straight to procedure instead of asking about that night. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she asked for a yes or no on whether anything is on his record right now, answer it in one word before you show the September in-class writing, because you went past her record point three times and she got sharper each time.
